title: Facilitated diffusion and active transport
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:31Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Facilitated diffusion and active transport
card: Many substances, such as ions and glucose, cannot easily cross the phospholipid part of the plasma membrane. They cross through transport proteins instead.
movement down a concentration gradient, from high to low, through a channel or carrier protein. It needs no energy from the cell.
movement against a concentration gradient, from low to high, through a carrier protein. It uses energy from ATP.
Both processes use proteins and are specific to the substance moved. The difference is the direction of movement and whether the cell must spend ATP.
draft.remember: Down the gradient with no ATP is facilitated. Against the gradient with ATP is active.

a.q: A cell takes in a mineral ion from soil water that has a lower concentration of the ion than the cell. Which process moves it?
opts: Facilitated diffusion, which needs no ATP
Active transport, which needs no ATP
a.why: The ion moves from low to high concentration, which is against the gradient. Only active transport does this, and it needs ATP. Facilitated diffusion is tempting because it also uses a protein, but it only moves substances down the gradient.
a.clue: Which way is the ion moving compared with the gradient?

b.q: A muscle cell has a low glucose level inside and a higher level outside. Glucose enters through a carrier protein, and the cell uses no ATP for this. What best describes the process?
opts: Facilitated diffusion, as glucose moves down its gradient
Active transport, as glucose moves through a protein
Simple diffusion, as glucose crosses the lipid part
Active transport, as glucose moves into the cell
b.why: Glucose moves from high outside to low inside, which is down its gradient, and no ATP is used. This is facilitated diffusion. Using a carrier protein does not make it active transport, because active transport needs ATP and moves substances against the gradient.
b.clue: Check the direction of the gradient and whether ATP is used.

b.best: Facilitated diffusion, as glucose moves down its gradient
